previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, and pacemaker was admitted for left neck redness, chills, and malaise following a TEE, concerning for cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin with rapid improvement and transitioned to oral doxycycline. During admission, she was diagnosed with recurrent C. difficile colitis based on a positive PCR, prompting initiation of a prolonged oral vancomycin course. Her warfarin dose was increased from 2 mg to 3 mg daily due to a persistently subtherapeutic INR of 1.4. She remained euvolemic on home diuretics, with stable heart failure and well-controlled atrial fibrillation. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics for both cellulitis and C. difficile, with instructions to follow up on anticoagulation and avoid loperamide until cleared by her primary care provider.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,
You were hospitalized due to symptoms of transient vertigo 
resulting from an TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACK, a condition where a 
blood vessel providing oxygen and nutrients to the brain is 
blocked by a clot. The brain is the part of your body that 
controls and directs all the other parts of your body, so damage 
to the brain from being deprived of its blood supply can result 
in a variety of symptoms.
Stroke can have many different causes, so we assessed you for 
medical conditions that might raise your risk of having stroke. 
In order to prevent future strokes, we plan to modify those risk 
factors. Your risk factors are:
atrial fibrillation

We are changing your medications as follows:
Increase your Coumadin
STOP aspirin
Please take your other medications as prescribed.

Please follow up with Neurology and your primary care physician 
as listed below.

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

If you experience any of the symptoms below, please seek 
emergency medical attention by calling Emergency Medical 
Services (dialing 911). In particular, since stroke can recur, 
please pay attention to the sudden onset and persistence of 
these symptoms:
- Sudden partial or complete loss of vision
- Sudden loss of the ability to speak words from your mouth
- Sudden loss of the ability to understand others speaking to 
you
- Sudden weakness of one side of the body
- Sudden drooping of one side of the face
- Sudden loss of sensation of one side of the body

Sincerely,
Your ___ Neurology Team

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CTA HEAD AND CTA NECK Q16 CT NECK

INDICATION:  ___ patient with left arm numbness, dizziness, TIA. 
Evaluate for acute intracranial hemorrhage, large territorial infarct,
dissection,  aneurysm,  or steno-occlusive disease.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous MDCT axial images were obtained through the brain
without contrast material. Subsequently, helically acquired rapid axial
imaging was performed from the aortic arch through the brain during the
infusion of 70 mL of Omnipaque intravenous contrast material.
Three-dimensional angiographic volume rendered, curved reformatted and
segmented images were generated on a dedicated workstation. This report is
based on interpretation of all of these images.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Sequenced Acquisition 6.4 s, 16.0 cm; CTDIvol = 56.1 mGy (Head) DLP =
897.1 mGy-cm.
   2) Stationary Acquisition 6.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 70.8 mGy (Head) DLP =
35.4 mGy-cm.
   3) Spiral Acquisition 5.2 s, 40.6 cm; CTDIvol = 31.9 mGy (Head) DLP =
1,296.9 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 2,229 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  ___ brain MRI, ___ head CT

FINDINGS: 

Study is limited secondary to patient body habitus and surgical hardware
streak artifact.

CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST:
There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, edema, or midline shift.
There is mild diffuse parenchymal volume loss with prominence of the sulci and
cisterns.  Focal right frontal lobe hypodensity is unchanged from ___ head CT. The ventricles are normal in size.  There is partial bilateral
ethmoid and maxillary sinus mucosal opacification.  The bilateral mastoid air
cells appear clear.

CTA HEAD:
There is a left dominant vertebral artery with mild vascular calcifications of
the V4 segment.  There is hypoplastic right vertebral artery, with possible
continuation into the right ___.  There are mild bilateral cavernous carotid
artery vascular calcifications.  There is a fetal type right posterior
cerebral artery.  Otherwise, the visualized circle of ___ and the principal
intracranial vasculature appear patent without stenosis, occlusion, or
aneurysm formation.  The dural venous sinuses appear patent.

CTA NECK:
There is common origin of the brachiocephalic and left carotid artery.  There
is a medial retropharyngeal course of the right ICA.  There is a left dominant
cervical vertebral artery.  The bilateral common and internal carotid arteries
appear patent without internal carotid artery stenosis by NASCET criteria. 
There are mild aortic arch vascular calcifications.

OTHER:
There is a left chest wall pacemaker device.  Sternotomy wires are visualized.
The thyroid gland appears heterogeneous, with streak artifact limiting
evaluation.  There is no lymphadenopathy per size criteria.  There are
multilevel degenerative changes of the cervical spine.  There is elevation of
the right hemidiaphragm.

IMPRESSION:


1. Study is limited secondary to patient body habitus and surgical hardware
streak artifact.
2. No evidence of acute large territorial infarction, acute intracranial
hemorrhage hemorrhage, or edema.  Please note MRI of the brain is more
sensitive for the detection of acute infarct.
3. Mild vascular calcifications without definite evidence of stenosis,
occlusion, or aneurysm formation.
4. Paranasal sinus disease as above.
